title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1971-02-24
lineage: Jace's DAT (48 KHz) playback on Sony PCM-R500, AES digital output > Benchmark DAC1, XLR analog output > Grace Lunatec V3, sample rate at 96 KHz, AES digiout) > AES digital input, professional mode/sync - LynxTwo soundcard in E6400 dual core processor-based PC > HD as 24 bit/96 KHz WAV > Ozone 3.0 > MBIT+ dithering to 16/44.1 KHz WAV > CDWAV 1.9 (tracking) > FLAC (level 8).   Recording, editing and mastering with Wavelab 5.0.  All cables were Mogami Gold 0.3m pro-audio XLR cables.  All components in the transfer/mastering chain were powered from a Cyberpower 1285AVR noise-attenuated uninterruptible AC power supply.
taper: Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer.
source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out > Fostex D5 @ 48 kHz > WBOTB Master DAT (DAT-1).

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a low‑energy 1971 show with strong first‑set moments (Cumberland, Bird Song) but an overall subdued performance.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard transfer that most listeners find clear and well‑balanced, though a few note minor pitch quirks and occasional channel swaps. Musically the concert is marked by a handful of highlights – notably a fiery "Cumberland," a beautiful "Bird Song" and a superb "Lovelight" – but the band’s energy wanes through much of the night, making it feel like the weakest outing of the six‑night run.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating (~3.5) with a split between enthusiastic praise for specific songs and criticism of overall low energy; recording quality is generally good but has noted technical quirks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp transfer praised by several reviewers; some mention pitch inconsistencies, channel swaps and speed adjustments needed for certain tracks, but no major drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens strong with Me & My Uncle and a blazing Cumberland, then drifts into quieter, less focused material; second set starts sluggish (King Bee) but picks up toward the end with the NFA/GDTRFB suite.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's playing described as choppy early on but later pushes hard, especially during the NFA/GDTRFB outro and adds wah‑infused phrasing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is noted as buried in the mix and generally subdued, though he steps up briefly during a Hard to Handle instrumental.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is mentioned slashing behind Garcia on Hard to Handle; otherwise no specific comments.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s absence is felt throughout, contributing to the listless vibe; drummers attempt to seg back into NFA toward the end.
